requirement:
The Rust outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Functions, methods, and function signatures | `fn` | Declared name |
| Structs, enums, unions, and traits | `struct`, `enum`, `union`, `trait` | Declared name |
| Implementations | `impl` | Written self type and optional trait path |
| Modules | `mod` | Declared name |
| Macro definitions | `macro` | Declared name |
| Macro invocations in item position | `macro` | Anonymous |
| Constants and statics | `const`, `static` | Declared name |
| Type aliases and associated types | `type` | Declared name |
| Foreign blocks | `extern` | ABI string, or `Rust` when absent |
| Extern-crate declarations | `extern-crate` | Declared name |
| Imports | `use` | Anonymous |

An implementation of `Trait` for `Thing` uses `impl[Thing/Trait]`;
an inherent implementation uses `impl[Thing]`. Nesting follows source
containment within the file. Outer attributes and outer documentation comments
attach to the following item; inner documentation comments belong to their
containing item or file root.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
The tests I reviewed cover every row of the item table and the attachment rules in `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.items`. I did not read the implementation, and I found no unacknowledged gap. Selector duplicate-name suffixes, percent encoding and anonymous hashes are delegated to `requirements.references.outline_selectors`, which is cited rather than reassessed here.

**Table rows**
- **Functions, methods and signatures (`fn`):**
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` asserts free functions (`fn[outer]`), methods (`impl[Thing]/fn[run]`), trait signatures (`trait[Trait]/fn[read]`) and foreign signatures (`extern[C]/fn[puts]`).
  - It also asserts nested functions (`fn[outer]/fn[inner]`).
- **Structs, enums, unions and traits:** the same test asserts `struct[Thing]`, `enum[E]`, `union[U]` and `trait[Trait]`.
- **Implementations:**
  - The tests assert `impl[Thing]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]`, the percent-encoded written self type `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`, and a generic form `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` (`#fn[item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not]`).
  - The inherent versus trait distinction is covered.
- **Modules:** `mod[local]` (inline) and `mod[external]` (declaration only) are asserted.
- **Macro definitions:** `macro[make]` is asserted.
- **Macro invocations in item position:**
  - `#fn[item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not]` checks that top-level, in-impl and in-mod invocations are anonymous, with the form `macro@<12 hex>`.
  - The same test checks that macros inside function bodies produce no nodes (7 selectors in total).
- **Constants and statics:** `const[C]` and `static[S]` are asserted.
- **Type aliases and associated types:** `type[Alias]` and `trait[Trait]/type[Item]` are asserted.
- **Foreign blocks:** `extern[C]` for an explicit ABI string and `extern[Rust]` when it is absent are both asserted.
- **Extern-crate declarations:** `extern-crate[core]` is asserted.
- **Imports:** `#fn[anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes]` and `#fn[selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates]` assert that `use` nodes are anonymous (`use@` plus 12 hex digits) and distinct.

**Nesting and attachment**
- **Nesting:** nested selectors in these tests, and the exact selector, kind and parent order in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes]`, cover containment.
- **Outer attributes and docs:** the `outline_content.rs` test asserts that the `fn[check]` span starts at `/// Check tokens.` and includes `#[inline]`.
- **Inner docs:** `#fn[comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container]` and `#fn[file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root]` assert that `//!` and `/*! */` comments belong to the containing `mod[m]` or to the root.
- **Outer comments:** the same tests assert that outer comments go to the next item.

**Residual observation**
- No test uses a path-qualified or generic trait in an impl selector, such as `impl fmt::Display for X`. The traits tested are `Trait` and `Trait` for `Wrapper<T>`.
- The self type is tested with generic and array forms.
- I did not treat the trait-path form as a separate required distinction. The requirement states no rule for it beyond "written" self type and "optional trait path".

I conclude that the tests adequately check the subject.

:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
